<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Among the reasons the Company acquired Zeltiq and the factors that contributed to the recognition of goodwill was the expansion of the Company&#8217;s leading medical aesthetics portfolio.&#160; Goodwill from the Zeltiq Acquisition of $<font style="color:#000000;">954.7 </font>million was assigned to the US Specialized Therapeutic segment and goodwill of $256.9 million was assigned to the International segment and is non-deductible for tax purposes.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Inventories </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of inventories acquired included an acquisition accounting fair market value step-up of $22.9 million which was recognized as a component of cost of sales as the inventory acquired was sold to the Company&#8217;s customers in the year ended December 31, 2017.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred Tax Liabilities</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred tax liabilities result from identifiable intangible assets&#8217; fair value adjustments. These adjustments create excess book basis over tax basis which is tax-effected by the statutory tax rates of applicable jurisdictions.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">LifeCell Corporation</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On February 1, 2017, the Company acquired LifeCell Corporation (&#8220;LifeCell&#8221;), a regenerative medicine company, for an acquisition accounting price of $2,883.1 million (the &#8220;LifeCell Acquisition&#8221;). The LifeCell Acquisition combined LifeCell's novel, regenerative medicines business, including its high-quality and durable portfolio of dermal matrix products with the Company's leading portfolio of medical aesthetic products, breast implants and tissue expanders. The LifeCell Acquisition expanded the Company&#8217;s medical aesthetics portfolio by adding Alloderm<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> and Strattice<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.27%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets Acquired and Liabilities Assumed at Fair Value</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The LifeCell Acquisition has been accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-31</a></p>

<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">IPR&amp;D and Intangible Assets</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of the acquired intangible assets was determined using the IPR&amp;D and Intangible Asset Valuation Technique. The discount rate used to arrive at the present value for these acquired intangible assets was 7.5% to reflect the internal rate of return and incremental commercial uncertainty in the cash flow projections in the LifeCell Acquisition. The discount rate of the LifeCell Acquisition was driven by the life-cycle stage of the products including, the advanced nature of IPR&amp;D projects and the therapeutic indication. For these and other reasons, actual results may vary significantly from estimated results.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following table identifies the summarized amounts recognized and the weighted average useful lives using the economic benefit of intangible assets ($ in millions):</p>

<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Among the reasons the Company acquired LifeCell and the factors that contributed to the recognition of goodwill was the expansion of the Company&#8217;s leading medical aesthetic portfolio.&#160; Goodwill from the LifeCell Acquisition of $<font style="color:#000000;">1,449.1 </font>million was assigned to the US Specialized Therapeutic segment and is non-deductible for tax purposes.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Inventories </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of inventories acquired included an acquisition accounting fair market value step-up of $108.4 million which was recognized as a component of cost of sales as the inventory acquired was sold to the Company&#8217;s customers in the year ended December 31, 2017, excluding currency impact.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-32</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU120"></a><font style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred Tax Liabilities</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred tax liabilities result from identifiable intangible assets&#8217; fair value adjustments. These adjustments create excess book basis over tax basis which is tax-effected by the statutory tax rates of applicable jurisdictions.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.27%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Licenses and Other Transactions Accounted for as Asset Acquisitions</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Lyndra, Inc.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On July 31, 2017, the Company entered into a collaboration, option and license agreement with Lyndra, Inc. (&#8220;Lyndra&#8221;) to develop orally administered ultra-long-acting (once-weekly) products for the treatment of Alzheimer&#8217;s disease and an additional, unspecified indication. The total upfront payment of $15.0 million was included as a component of R&amp;D expense in the year ended December 31, 2017. The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets, the lack of acquired employees and manufacturing, as well as the lack of certain other inputs and processes, that the transaction did not qualify as a business.&nbsp;&nbsp;The future option exercise payments, if any, and any future success based milestones relating to the licensed products of up to $85.0 million will be recorded if the corresponding events become probable.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Editas Medicine, Inc.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On March 14, 2017, the Company entered into a strategic alliance and option agreement with Editas Medicine, Inc. (&#8220;Editas&#8221;) for access to early stage, first-in-class eye care programs. Pursuant to the agreement, Allergan made an upfront payment of $90.0 million for the right to license up to five of Editas&#8217; gene-editing programs in eye care, including its lead program for Leber Congenital Amaurosis (&#8220;LCA&#8221;). Under the terms of the agreement, if an option is exercised, Editas is eligible to receive contingent research and development and commercial milestones plus royalties based on net sales.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets, the lack of acquired employees and manufacturing, as well as the lack of certain other inputs and processes, that the transaction did not qualify as a business. The total upfront payment of $90.0 million was included as a component of R&amp;D expense in the year ended December 31, 2017. The future option exercise payments, if any, and any future success based milestones relating to the licensed products will be recorded if the corresponding events become probable.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In the year ended December 31, 2018, the Company exercised a $15.0 million option to develop and commercialize EDIT-101 globally for the treatment of LCA10 which was included as a component of R&amp;D expense.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, Editas has exercised its option to co-develop and share equally in the profits and losses from EDIT-101 in the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;Editas received an additional $25.0 million milestone, which was included as a component as R&amp;D expense in the year ended December 31, 2018, as the FDA accepted the investigational new drug application for EDIT-101.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assembly Biosciences, Inc.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 9, 2017, the Company entered into a licensing agreement with Assembly Biosciences, Inc. (&#8220;Assembly&#8221;) for the worldwide rights to Assembly&#8217;s microbiome gastrointestinal development programs. Under the terms of the agreement, the Company made an upfront payment to Assembly of $50.0 million for the exclusive, worldwide rights to develop and commercialize certain development compounds. Additionally, Assembly will be eligible to receive success-based development and commercial milestone payments plus royalties based on net sales. The Company and Assembly will generally share development costs through proof-of-concept (&#8220;POC&#8221;) studies, and Allergan will assume all post-POC development costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets, the lack of acquired employees and manufacturing as well as the lack of certain other inputs and processes that the transaction did not qualify as a business.&nbsp;&nbsp;The total upfront payment of $50.0 million was included as a component of R&amp;D expense in the year ended December 31, 2017 and the future success based milestone payments of up to $2,771.0 million, including amounts for additional development programs not committed to as of December 31, 2017, will be recorded if the corresponding events become probable.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Lysosomal Therapeutics, Inc.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 9, 2017, the Company entered into a definitive agreement for the option to acquire Lysosomal Therapeutics, Inc. (&#8220;LTI&#8221;). LTI is focused on innovative small-molecule research and development in the field of neurodegeneration, yielding new treatment options for patients with severe neurological diseases. Under the agreement, Allergan acquired an option right directly from LTI shareholders to acquire LTI for $150.0 million plus future milestone payments following completion of a Phase Ib trial for LTI-291 as well as an upfront research and development payment. The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets, the lack of acquired employees and manufacturing, as well as the lack of certain other inputs and processes, that the transaction did not qualify as a business. The aggregate upfront payment of $145.0 million was recorded as a component of R&amp;D expense in the year ended December 31, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company did not exercise its option and on January 2, 2019, the option agreement with LTI was terminated.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-33</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU121"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other Transactions</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On September 8, 2017, the Company entered into an agreement with the Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe, under which the Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe obtained the rights to Orange Book-listed patents covering Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> (Cyclosporine Ophthalmic Emulsion) 0.05%, and the Company was granted exclusive licenses under the patents related to the product. Pursuant to the agreement, the Company paid the Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe an upfront payment of $13.8 million, which was recorded as a component of cost of sales in the year ended December 31, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe will be eligible to receive up to $15.0 million in annual royalties starting in 2018, during the period that certain patent claims remain in effect.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2016 Significant Business Developments<font style="font-style:normal;"> </font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following are the significant transactions that were completed in the year ended December&#160;31, 2016. Refer to &#8220;NOTE 8 &#8212; Discontinued Operations&#8221; for material divestitures that were completed into during the year ended December 31, 2016.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.27%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Acquisitions</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Tobira<font style="font-style:normal;">&#160;</font>Therapeutics, Inc. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On November 1, 2016, the Company&#160;acquired&#160;Tobira&#160;Therapeutics, Inc.&#160;(&#8220;Tobira&#8221;), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing therapies for non-alcoholic&#160;steatohepatitis&#160;(&#8220;NASH&#8221;) and other liver diseases for&#160;an acquisition accounting purchase price of $570.1 million, plus contingent consideration of up to $49.84 per share in&#160;contingent value rights&#160;(&#8220;CVR&#8221;), or up to $1,101.3 million,&#160;that may be payable based on the successful completion of certain development, regulatory and commercial milestones (the &#8220;Tobira&#160;Acquisition&#8221;), of which $303.1 million was paid in the year ended December 31, 2017 for the initiation of Phase III clinical trials. The CVR had an acquisition date fair value of $479.0 million. The Tobira Acquisition added Cenicriviroc, a differentiated, complementary development program for the treatment of the multi-factorial elements of NASH, including inflammation, metabolic syndromes and fibrosis, to Allergan's global gastroenterology R&amp;D pipeline. </p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.26%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets Acquired and Liabilities Assumed at Fair Value</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">IPR&amp;D and Intangible Assets</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of the IPR&amp;D intangible assets was determined using the IPR&amp;D and Intangible Asset Valuation Technique. The discount rate used to arrive at the present value for IPR&amp;D intangible assets was 11.5% to reflect the internal rate of return and incremental commercial uncertainty in the cash flow projections. The discount rate of the acquisition was driven by the stage of the product and the therapeutic indication. No assurances can be given that the underlying assumptions used to prepare the discounted cash flow analysis will not change. For these and other reasons, actual results may vary significantly from estimated results.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-34</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU122"></a><font style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Among the reasons the Company acquired Tobira and the factors that contributed to the recognition of goodwill was the expansion of the Company&#8217;s pipeline of NASH products.&#160; Goodwill from the Tobira Acquisition of $98.6 million was assigned to the US General Medicine segment and is non-deductible for tax purposes.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Contingent Consideration</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As part of the acquisition, the Company is required to pay the former shareholders of Tobira up to $1,101.3 million,&#160;of which $303.1 million was paid in the year ended December 31, 2017, based on the timing of the certain development, regulatory and commercial milestones, if any.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the time of the acquisition, the Company estimated the fair value of the contingent consideration to be $479.0 million using a probability weighted average approach that considered the possible outcomes of scenarios related to the specified product.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred Tax Liabilities</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred tax liabilities result from identifiable intangible assets&#8217; fair value adjustments. These adjustments create excess book basis over tax basis which is tax-effected by the statutory tax rates of applicable jurisdictions.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Vitae Pharmaceuticals, Inc.<font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;"> </font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On October 25, 2016, the Company&#160;acquired&#160;Vitae Pharmaceuticals, Inc.&#160;(&#8220;Vitae&#8221;), a clinical-stage&#160;biotechnology company, for&#160;an acquisition accounting purchase price of $621.4 million&#160;(the &#8220;Vitae&#160;Acquisition&#8221;). At the time of the transaction, the Vitae Acquisition&#160;was anticipated to expand&#160;Allergan&#8217;s dermatology product pipeline with the addition of a Phase II orally active&#160;RORyt&#160;(retinoic acid receptor-related orphan receptor gamma) inhibitor for the potential treatment of psoriasis and other autoimmune disorders, and a Phase II atopic dermatitis drug candidate.&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets Acquired and Liabilities Assumed at Fair Value</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-35</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU123"></a><font style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">IPR&amp;D and Intangible Assets</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of the IPR&amp;D intangible assets was determined using the IPR&amp;D and Intangible Asset Valuation Technique. The discount rate used to arrive at the present value for IPR&amp;D intangible assets was 9.5% to reflect the internal rate of return and incremental commercial uncertainty in the cash flow projections. The discount rate of the acquisition was driven by the stage of the product and the therapeutic indication.&nbsp;&nbsp;Refer to &#8220;NOTE 16 &#8211; Goodwill, Product Rights and Other Intangible Assets&#8221; for impairments of the acquired assets.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Among the reasons the Company acquired Vitae and the factors that contributed to the recognition of goodwill was the expansion of the Company&#8217;s pipeline of dermatology products.&#160; Goodwill from the Vitae Acquisition of $30.6 million was assigned to the US Specialized Therapeutic segment and is non-deductible for tax purposes.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred Tax Liabilities</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred tax liabilities result from identifiable intangible assets&#8217; fair value adjustments. These adjustments create excess book basis over tax basis which is tax-effected by the statutory tax rates of applicable jurisdictions.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets Held for Sale</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company held for sale certain intangible assets acquired as part of the Vitae Acquisition.&#160; These assets had an acquisition accounting value of $22.5 million. In the year ended December 31, 2017, the Company sold these assets for $22.5 million. </p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ForSight VISION5, Inc.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On September 23, 2016, the Company acquired ForSight VISION5, Inc. (&#8220;ForSight&#8221;), a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on eye care, in an all cash transaction of approximately $95.0 million (the &#8220;ForSight Acquisition&#8221;). Under the terms of the ForSight Acquisition, the Company acquired ForSight for an acquisition accounting purchase price of $74.5 million plus the payment of outstanding indebtedness of $14.8 million and other miscellaneous charges. ForSight shareholders are eligible to receive contingent consideration of up to $125.0 million, which had an initial estimated fair value of $79.8 million, relating to commercialization milestones. The Company acquired ForSight for its lead development program, a peri-ocular ring designed for extended drug delivery and reducing elevated intraocular pressure (&#8220;IOP&#8221;) in glaucoma patients. </p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.27%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets Acquired and Liabilities Assumed at Fair Value</p>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following table summarizes the fair values of the assets acquired and liabilities assumed at the acquisition date ($ in millions):</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-36</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU124"></a><font style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">IPR&amp;D and Intangible Assets</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of the IPR&amp;D intangible assets was determined using the IPR&amp;D and Intangible Asset Valuation Technique. The discount rate used to arrive at the present value for IPR&amp;D intangible assets was 13.0% to reflect the internal rate of return and incremental commercial uncertainty in the cash flow projections. The discount rate of the acquisition was driven by the early stage of the product and the therapeutic indication. No assurances can be given that the underlying assumptions used to prepare the discounted cash flow analysis will not change. For these and other reasons, actual results may vary significantly from estimated results.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.27%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Among the reasons the Company acquired ForSight and the factors that contributed to the recognition of goodwill was the expansion of the Company&#8217;s pipeline of eye care products.&nbsp;&nbsp;Goodwill from the ForSight Acquisition of $50.5 million was assigned to the US Specialized Therapeutics segment and is non-deductible for tax purposes.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.27%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Contingent Consideration</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As part of the acquisition, the Company is required to pay the former shareholders of ForSight up to $125.0 million based on the timing of the first commercial sale, if any.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company estimated the fair value of the contingent consideration to be $79.8 million using a probability weighted average approach that considered the possible outcomes of scenarios related to the specified product. In the year ended December 31, 2016, t<font style="color:#000000;">he Company recognized approximately&#160;$33.0 million in impairments of the acquired&#160;ForSight&#160;IPR&amp;D asset as the Company anticipated a delay in potential launch timing, if any.&#160;&#160;Offsetting&#160;this impairment was a corresponding reduction of acquired contingent consideration of $15.0 million, which reduced overall R&amp;D expenses.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.27%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU137"></a>Deferred Tax Liabilities</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred tax liabilities result from identifiable intangible assets&#8217; fair value adjustments. These adjustments create excess book basis over tax basis which is tax-effected by the statutory tax rates of applicable jurisdictions.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.27%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Licenses and Asset Acquisitions</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Motus&#160;Therapeutics, Inc.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On&#160;December&#160;15, 2016, the Company&#160;acquired&#160;Motus&#160;Therapeutics, Inc. (&#8220;Motus&#8221;) for&#160;an upfront payment of approximately&#160;$200.0 million (the &#8220;Motus&#160;Transaction&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Motus&#160;has the worldwide rights&#160;to RM-131 (relamorelin), a peptide ghrelin agonist being developed for the treatment of diabetic&#160;gastroparesis.&#160; Under the terms of the Motus Transaction,&#160;Motus&#160;shareholders are eligible to receive contingent consideration in connection with the commercial launch of the product.&#160;The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets, the lack of acquired employees as well as certain other inputs and processes that the transaction&#160;did not qualify as a business.&#160;The total upfront net payment of&#160;$199.5&#160;million was included as a component of R&amp;D expense in the year ended December 31, 2016 and the future milestone will be recorded if the corresponding event becomes probable.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Chase Pharmaceuticals <font style="color:#000000;">Corporation</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On November 22, 2016, the Company&#160;acquired Chase Pharmaceuticals Corporation (&#8220;Chase&#8221;),&#160;a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on&#160;the development of improved treatments for neurodegenerative disorders including Alzheimer's disease,&#160;for an upfront payment of&#160;approximately&#160;$125.0&#160;million&#160;plus potential regulatory and commercial milestones of up to $875.0 million&#160;related to Chase's lead compound, CPC-201, and certain backup compounds&#160;(the &#8220;Chase Transaction&#8221;).&#160;The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets, the lack of acquired employees as well as certain other inputs and processes that the Chase Transaction did not qualify as a business. The total upfront net payment of $122.9 million was expensed as a component of R&amp;D expense in the year ended December 31, 2016 and the future milestones will be recorded if the corresponding events become probable.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the year ended December 31, 2018, milestone payments of $75.0 million were included as a component of R&amp;D expense.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-37</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU125"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AstraZeneca</font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;plc </font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">License</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On October 2, 2016, the Company entered into a licensing agreement with&#160;MedImmune, AstraZeneca plc's (&#8220;AstraZeneca&#8221;) global biologics research and development arm, for the global rights to&#160;brazikumab&#160;(the &#8220;AstraZeneca Transaction&#8221;).&#160;Brazikumab&#160;is an anti-IL-23 monoclonal antibody for the treatment of patients with moderate-to-severe&#160;Crohn's&#160;disease and was Phase II ready for ulcerative colitis and other conditions treated with anti-IL-23 monoclonal antibodies.&#160; Under the terms of the AstraZeneca Transaction, AstraZeneca received&#160;$250.0 million for the exclusive, worldwide license to develop and commercialize&#160;brazikumab&#160;and can receive contingent consideration of up to $1.27 billion (as of the time of the transaction), as well as tiered royalties on sales of the product.&#160;The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets, the lack of acquired employees and manufacturing as well as certain other inputs and processes that the transaction did not qualify as a business. The total upfront payment of $250.0 million was included as a component of R&amp;D expense in the year ended December 31, 2016 and the future milestones will be recorded if the corresponding events become probable.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the year ended December 31, 2018, milestones of $90.0 million, related to the probable initiation of clinical studies, were expensed as a component of R&amp;D expense.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">RetroSense Therapeutics, LLC</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On September 6, 2016, the Company acquired certain assets of&#160;RetroSense&#160;Therapeutics LLC (&#8220;RetroSense&#8221;),&#160;a private, clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on novel gene therapy approaches to restore vision in patients suffering from blindness (the &#8220;RetroSense&#160;Transaction&#8221;). Under the terms of the RetroSense Transaction,&#160;RetroSense&#160;received approximately $60.0 million upfront, and is eligible to receive up to $495.0 million in contingent regulatory and commercialization milestone payments related to its lead development program, RST-001, a novel gene therapy for the treatment of retinitis&#160;pigmentosa.&#160;&#160;The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets, the lack of acquired employees as well as certain other inputs and processes that the RetroSense Transaction did not qualify as a business.&#160; The total upfront net payment of $59.7 million was included as a component of R&amp;D expense in the year ended December 31, 2016 and the future milestones will be recorded if the corresponding events become probable.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Akarna Therapeutics, Ltd.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On August 26, 2016, the Company acquired&#160;Akarna&#160;Therapeutics, Ltd. (&#8220;Akarna&#8221;), a biopharmaceutical company developing novel small molecule therapeutics that target inflammatory and fibrotic diseases (the &#8220;Akarna&#160;Transaction&#8221;). Under the terms of the Akarna Transaction,&#160;Akarna&#160;shareholders received approximately $50.0 million upfront and were eligible to receive contingent development and commercialization milestones of up to $1,015.0 million.&#160;The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets as well as a lack of certain other inputs and processes that the Akarna Transaction did not qualify as a business.&#160; The total upfront net payment of $48.2 million was included as a component of R&amp;D expense <font style="color:#000000;">in the year ended December 31, 2016</font> and the future milestones will be recorded if the corresponding events become probable.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the year ended December 31, 2017, a milestone of $39.6 million, related to the initiation of a clinical study, was included as a component of R&amp;D expense.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Topokine Therapeutics, Inc.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On April 21, 2016, the Company acquired Topokine Therapeutics, Inc. (&#8220;Topokine&#8221;), a privately held, clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on development stage topical medicines for fat reduction (the &#8220;Topokine Transaction&#8221;). Under the terms of the Topokine Transaction, Topokine shareholders received an upfront payment of $85.8 million and are eligible to receive contingent development and commercialization milestones of up to $260.0 million for XAF5, a first-in-class topical agent in development for the treatment of steatoblepharon, also known as undereye bags.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets, the lack of acquired employees as well as certain other inputs and processes that the Topokine Transaction did not qualify as a business.&nbsp;&nbsp;The total upfront net payment of approximately $85.0 million was included as a component of R&amp;D expense <font style="color:#000000;">in the year ended December 31, 2016</font> and the future milestones will be recorded if the corresponding events become probable.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Heptares Therapeutics, Ltd.</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On April 6, 2016, the Company entered into an agreement with&#160;Heptares&#160;Therapeutics, Ltd. (&#8220;Heptares&#8221;), under which the Company licensed exclusive global rights to a portfolio of novel subtype-selective muscarinic receptor agonists in development for the treatment of major neurological disorders, including Alzheimer's disease (the &#8220;Heptares&#160;Transaction&#8221;). Under the terms of the Heptares Transaction,&#160;Heptares&#160;received an upfront payment of $125.0 million and is eligible to receive contingent milestone payments of up to approximately $665.0 million upon successful Phase I, II and III clinical development and launch of the first three licensed compounds for multiple indications and up to approximately $2.575 billion associated with achieving certain annual sales thresholds during the several years following launch. In addition,&#160;Heptares&#160;was eligible to receive contingent tiered royalties on net sales of all products resulting from the partnership.&#160;The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets, the lack of acquired employees as well as certain other inputs and processes that the Heptares Transaction did not qualify as a business. The total upfront payment of $125.0 million was included as a component of R&amp;D expense <font style="color:#000000;">in the year ended December 31, 2016</font> and the future milestones will be recorded if the events become probable.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the year ended December 31, 2017, a milestone of $15.0 million, related to the initiation of a clinical study, was included as a component of R&amp;D expense.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-38</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU126"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Anterios, Inc.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 6, 2016, the Company acquired&#160;Anterios, Inc. (&#8220;Anterios&#8221;), a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company developing a next generation delivery system and&#160;botulinum&#160;toxin-based prescription products (&#8220;the&#160;Anterios&#160;Transaction&#8221;). Under the terms of the Anterios Transaction,&#160;Anterios&#160;shareholders received an upfront net payment of approximately $90.0 million and are eligible to receive contingent development and&#160;commercialization milestone payments up to $387.5&#160;million related to an investigational topical formulation of&#160;botulinum&#160;toxin type A in development for the potential treatment of hyperhidrosis, acne, and crow&#8217;s feet lines and the related NDS&#8482;,&#160;Anterios' proprietary platform delivery technology that enables local, targeted delivery of neurotoxins through the skin without the need for injections.&#160;&#160;The Company concluded based on the stage of development of the assets, the lack of acquired employees as well as certain other inputs and processes that the Anterios Transaction did not qualify as a business.&#160; The total upfront net payment of $89.2 million was included as a component of R&amp;D expense <font style="color:#000000;">in the year ended December 31, 2016</font><font style="font-size:12pt;"> </font>and the future milestones will be recorded if the corresponding events become probable.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December 31, 2018, Allergan concluded that its Anti-Infectives business met the criteria for held for sale based on management&#8217;s intent and ability to divest the business within the next twelve months.&#160; As a result of this decision, Allergan impaired the business assets by $771.7 million, including goodwill of $622.0 million, based on the expected aggregate fair value to be received of approximately $885.0 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon the sale of the business, Allergan would only recognize the upfront proceeds received in exchange for the assets disposed, which may result in further potential write downs as of the date of sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;If contingent consideration is part of the aggregate fair value received, the Company would recognize any future benefits in &#8220;other income / (expense)&#8221; as the contingent portion of the divestiture is earned.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2017, assets held for sale principally consisted of facilities no longer in use and certain product rights and other intangibles and goodwill.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 7 &#8212; Collaborations </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has ongoing transactions with other entities through collaboration agreements. The following represent the material collaboration agreements impacting the years ended December&#160;31, 2018, 2017 and 2016.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Ironwood Collaboration</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In September 2007, Forest entered into a collaboration agreement with Ironwood Pharmaceuticals (&#8220;Ironwood&#8221;) to jointly develop and commercialize Linzess<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> (linaclotide) for the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) and chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC). Under the terms of the agreement, the Company shares equally with Ironwood all profits and losses (as defined) from the development and commercialization of Linzess in the U.S. In addition, the Company expanded this agreement to cover the acquired Constella rights internationally.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The agreement included contingent milestone payments as well as a contingent equity investment based on the achievement of specific clinical and commercial milestones. The Company may be obligated to pay up to an additional $100.0 million if certain sales milestones are achieved.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-39</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU127"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Based on the nature of the arrangement (including its contractual terms), the nature of the payments and applicable guidance, the Company records receipts from and payments to Ironwood in two pools: the &#8220;Development pool&#8221; which consists of R&amp;D expenses, and the &#8220;Commercialization pool,&#8221; which consists of revenue, cost of sales and other operating expenses. The net payment to or receipt from Ironwood for the Development pool is recorded in R&amp;D expense and the net payment to or receipt from Ironwood for the Commercialization pool is recorded in cost of goods sold.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the year ended December 31, 2018, the Company recorded a </font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">$29.9 million Linzess</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> profit share true-up in cost of sales.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Amgen Collaboration </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In December 2011, we entered into a collaboration agreement with Amgen Inc. (&#8220;Amgen&#8221;) to develop and commercialize, on a worldwide basis, biosimilar versions of Herceptin<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>, Avastin<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>, Rituxan/Mab Thera<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>, and Erbitux<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> (the &#8220;Amgen Collaboration Agreement&#8221;). Amgen has assumed primary responsibility for developing, manufacturing and initially commercializing the oncology antibody products.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition, we will contribute our significant expertise in the commercialization and marketing of products in highly competitive specialty markets, including helping effectively manage the lifecycle of the biosimilar products. The collaboration products are expected to be sold under a joint Amgen/Allergan label. We will initially receive royalties and sales milestones from product revenues. The collaboration will not pursue biosimilars of Amgen&#8217;s proprietary products.&#160; In the year ended December 31, 2017, the FDA approved MVASI &#8482;, a biosimilar of Avastin, for the treatment of five types of cancer.&#160; As a result of the approval, the Company can achieve certain commercial and sales based milestones and receive royalties based on the net sales of the product.&#160; In the year ended December 31, 2018, the Company recorded $25.0 million in milestone revenue as a result of the anticipated product launch of MVASI<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#8482;</sup> during the 2019 fiscal year.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, in the year ended December 31, 2018, the European Commission granted marketing authorization for MVASI <sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#8482;</sup> and KANJINTI<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#8482;</sup>, both biosimilars of Herceptin.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE&#160;8 &#8212; Discontinued Operations </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Global Generics Business</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On July 27, 2015, the Company announced that it entered into the Teva Transaction, which closed on August 2, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;On October 3, 2016, the Company completed the divestiture of the Anda Distribution business to Teva for $500.0 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recognized a combined gain on the sale of the Anda Distribution business and the sale of the global generics business of $15,932.2 million in the twelve months ended December 31, 2016.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In October 2016, pursuant to our agreement with Teva, Teva provided the Company with its proposed estimated adjustment to the closing date working capital balance.&#160; The Company disagreed with Teva&#8217;s proposed adjustment, and, pursuant to our agreement with Teva, each of the Company&#8217;s and Teva&#8217;s proposed adjustments were submitted to arbitration (&#8220;Working Capital Arbitration&#8221;) to determine the working capital amount in accordance with GAAP as applied by the Company consistent with past practice.&nbsp;&nbsp;On January 31, 2018, Allergan plc and Teva entered into a Settlement Agreement and Mutual Releases (the &#8220;Agreement&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Agreement provides that the Company will make a one-time payment of $700.0 million to Teva which was paid in the year ended December 31, 2018; the Company and Teva will jointly dismiss their working capital dispute arbitration, and the Company and Teva will release all actual or potential claims under the Master Purchase Agreement, dated July 26, 2015, by and between the Company and Teva, for breach of any representation, warranty, or covenant (other than any breach of a post-closing covenant not known as of the date of the Agreement).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recorded a pre-tax charge of $466.0 million as a component of other (expense) / income, net from discontinued operations relating to the settlement in the year ended December 31, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company notes the following reconciliation of the proceeds received in the combined transaction to the gain recognized in income from discontinued operations in 2016 ($ in millions): </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 9 &#8212; Share-Based Compensation</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company recognizes compensation expense for all share-based compensation awards made to employees and directors based on the fair value of the awards on the date of grant. A summary of the Company&#8217;s share-based compensation plans is presented below.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Option award plans require options to be granted at the fair market value of the shares underlying the options at the date of the grant and generally become exercisable over periods ranging from three to five years. Each option granted expires ten years from the date of the grant. Restricted stock awards are grants that entitle the holder to ordinary shares, subject to certain terms. Restricted stock unit awards are grants that entitle the holder the right to receive an ordinary share, subject to certain terms. Restricted stock and restricted stock unit awards (both time-based vesting and performance-based vesting) generally have restrictions that lapse over a one to four year vesting period. Restrictions generally lapse for non-employee directors after one year. Certain restricted stock units are performance-based awards issued at a target number with the actual number of ordinary shares issued ranging based on achievement of the performance criteria.&nbsp;&nbsp;All restricted stock and restricted stock units which remain active under the Company&#8217;s equity award plans are eligible to receive cash dividend equivalent payments upon vesting.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair Value Assumptions</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">All restricted stock and restricted stock units (whether time-based or performance-based) are granted and expensed using the fair value per share on the applicable grant date, over the applicable vesting period. Non-qualified options to purchase ordinary shares are granted to employees at exercise prices per share equal to the closing market price per share on the date of grant. The fair value of non-qualified options is determined on the applicable grant dates using the Black-Scholes method of valuation and that amount is recognized as an expense over the vesting period. Using the Black-Scholes valuation model, the fair value of options is based on the following assumptions: </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 10 &#8212;&#160;Pension and Other Postretirement Benefit Plans </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Defined Benefit Plan Obligations</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has numerous defined benefit plans offered to employees around the world. For these plans, retirement benefits are generally based on an employee&#8217;s years of service and compensation. Funding requirements are determined on an individual country and plan basis and are subject to local country practices and market circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2018, all of the Company&#8217;s plans were frozen for future enrollment.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The service and settlement costs captured as part of the net periodic (benefit) are recorded within general &amp; administrative expenses and the interest costs and expected return on plan assets are recorded within &#8220;other income / (expense), net&#8221;.<font style="color:#FF0000;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>The net periodic (benefit) of the defined benefit plans for continuing operations for the years ended December&#160;31, 2018, 2017 and 2016 was as follows ($ in millions):</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The underfunding of pension benefits is primarily a function of the different funding incentives that exist outside of the United States. In certain countries, there are no legal requirements or financial incentives provided to companies to pre-fund pension obligations. In these instances, benefit payments are typically paid directly by the Company as they become due.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Plan Assets</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Companies are required to use a fair value hierarchy as defined in ASC 820 which maximizes the use of observable inputs and minimizes the use of unobservable inputs when measuring fair value (&#8220;Fair Value Leveling&#8221;). There are three levels of inputs used to measure fair value with Level 1 having the highest priority and Level 3 having the lowest:</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;1&#160;&#8212;&#160;Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;2&#160;&#8212;&#160;Observable inputs other than Level&#160;1 prices, such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities, or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the assets or liabilities.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;3&#160;&#8212;&#160;Unobservable inputs that are supported by little or no market activity. The Level 3 assets are those whose values are determined using pricing models, discounted cash flow methodologies, or similar techniques with significant unobservable inputs, as well as instruments for which the determination of fair value requires significant judgment or estimation.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">If the inputs used to measure the financial assets fall within more than one level described above, the categorization is based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement of the instrument.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-46</a></p>

<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Net (loss) / gain amounts reflect experience differentials primarily relating to differences between expected and actual returns on plan assets as well as the effects of changes in actuarial assumptions. Net loss amounts in excess of certain thresholds are amortized into net pension cost over the average remaining service life of employees. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In order to select a discount rate for purposes of valuing the plan obligations the Company uses market returns and adjusts them as needed to fit the estimated duration of the plan liabilities.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The expected rate of return represents the average rate of return to be earned on plan assets over the period the benefits included in the benefit obligation are to be paid. In developing the expected rate of return, long-term historical returns data are considered as well as actual returns on the plan assets and other capital markets experience. Using this reference information, the long-term return expectations for each asset category and a weighted average expected return was developed, according to the allocation among those investment categories.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other Post-Employment Benefit Plans</p>

<p style="margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Teva Share Activity</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Refer to &#8220;NOTE 8 &#8212; Discontinued Operations&#8221; for the movements that the Company recorded during the years ended December 31, 2018 and 2017 in its investment in Teva securities.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Sale of Business</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the year ended December 31, 2018, the Company recorded a net gain of $129.6 million as a result of the sale of five medical dermatology products to Almirall, S.A.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the year ended December 31, 2018, the Company completed the sale of a non-strategic asset group held for sale as of December 31, 2017, which was deemed a business based on the applicable guidance at the time, for $55.0 million in cash plus deferred consideration of $20.0 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of this transaction, the Company recognized a gain of $53.0 million.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Debt Extinguishment Costs as Part of the Debt Tender Offer</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On May 30, 2017, the Company completed the repurchase of certain debt securities issued for cash under a previously announced tender offer.<font style="font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>In the year ended December 31, 2017, as a result of the debt extinguishment,&nbsp;&nbsp;the Company repaid $2,843.3 million of senior notes and recognized a loss of $161.6 million, within &#8220;other (expense) / income, net&#8221; for the early tender payment and non-cash write-off of premiums and debt fees related to the repurchased notes, including $170.5 million of a make-whole premium.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;margin-left:2.27%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Debt Extinguishment Other</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the year ended December 31, 2018, the Company repurchased $3,939.1 million of senior notes in the open market.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of the debt extinguishment, the Company recognized a net gain of $15.6 million within &#8220;other income / (expense), net&#8221; for the discount received upon repurchase of $45.6 million, offset by the non-cash write-off of premiums and debt fees related to the repaid notes of $30.0 million.</p>
