<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">expires in 2033.) On October 20, 2017, November 30, 2017 and January 20, 2018, Plaintiffs brought actions for infringement of the &#8216;371 patent in </font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware against Teva, Mylan and Sandoz, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The actions filed in October and November 2017 against Teva and Mylan have been consolidated with the lawsuit filed in November 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In December 2017 and February 2018, subsidiaries of the Company and Ironwood received Paragraph IV certification notice letters from Teva and Mylan, respectively indicating that they had submitted to FDA ANDAs seeking approval to manufacture and sell generic versions of LINZESS<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> 72 mcg capsules (&#8220;72 mcg ANDA&#8221;) before the expiration of the &#8216;036, &#8216;727, &#8216;947, &#8216;409, &#8216;526, &#8216;553, &#8216;030 and &#8216;371 Patents. Teva and Mylan claim that these patents are invalid, unenforceable and/or would not be infringed. On February 2, 2018 and March 29, 2018, subsidiaries of the Company and Ironwood Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (collectively, &#8220;Plaintiffs&#8221;), brought actions for infringement of some or all of the &#8216;036, &#8216;727, &#8216;947, &#8216;409, &#8216;526, &#8216;553, &#8216;030 and &#8216;371 Patents in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware against Teva and Mylan, respectively. These lawsuits triggered automatic stays of approval of Teva&#8217;s 72 mcg ANDA and Mylan&#8217;s 72 mcg ANDA that expire no earlier than June 2020 and August 2020, respectively (unless there is a final court decision adverse to Plaintiffs sooner).&nbsp;&nbsp;On March 14, 2018, the district court consolidated the Teva 72 mcg ANDA matter with the lawsuit filed in November 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In May and August 2018, the district court granted joint stipulations and orders to dismiss without prejudice all claims, counterclaims, and defenses in the consolidated actions with respect to the &#8216;371 Patent and the &#8216;030 Patent, respectively,<font style="font-size:12pt;"> </font>as between Plaintiffs, Teva and Sandoz.&nbsp;&nbsp;On July 10, 2018, Plaintiffs filed a motion to dismiss all claims and declaratory judgment counterclaims between Plaintiffs and Mylan with respect to the &#8216;371 patent for lack of subject matter jurisdiction.&nbsp;&nbsp;On July 26, 2018, Plaintiffs filed a motion for leave to file an amended complaint as to Mylan to assert the &#8216;628 patent against Mylan&#8217;s 72 mcg ANDA product. On August 30, 2018, the district court entered an order granting the joint stipulation and order to dismiss without prejudice all claims, counterclaims, and defenses in the consolidated actions with respect to the &#8216;030 Patent and the &#8216;371 Patent as between Plaintiffs and Mylan, granting Plaintiffs&#8217; motion seeking leave to file an amended complaint, and withdrawing as moot Plaintiffs&#8217; motion to dismiss with respect to the &#8216;371 patent. Plaintiffs filed a corrected amended complaint as to Mylan on September 4, 2018, and Mylan filed an answer to the amended complaint on September 13, 2018.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On June 12, 2018, the district court granted the parties&#8217; request that briefing on Mylan&#8217;s motion to dismiss for improper venue be stayed until after a decision issued on Mylan&#8217;s renewed motion to dismiss for improper venue in <font style="font-style:italic;">Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. v. Mylan Pharmaceuticals, Inc.</font>, C.A. Nos. 17-374 (LPS), 17-379 (LPS) (&#8220;<font style="font-style:italic;">BMS</font>&#8221;). On October 18, 2018, the district court in <font style="font-style:italic;">BMS </font>granted Mylan&#8217;s motion to dismiss for improper venue in that case.  </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December 21, 2018, subsidiaries of the Company and Ironwood entered into a settlement agreement with Mylan. Under the terms of the settlement agreement, Plaintiffs will provide a license to Mylan to market a generic version of LINZESS in the United States beginning on February 5, 2030 (subject to FDA approval), or earlier in certain circumstances. The Mylan actions were dismissed on December 27, 2018.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Namenda XR<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>.  In 2014, subsidiaries of the Company brought actions for infringement of some or all of U.S. Patent Nos.&#160;5,061,703&#160;(the &#8220;&#8216;703 patent&#8221;), 8,039,009&#160;(the &#8220;&#8216;009 patent&#8221;), 8,168,209&#160;(the &#8220;&#8216;209 patent&#8221;), 8,173,708 (the &#8220;&#8216;708 patent&#8221;),&#160;8,283,379&#160;(the &#8220;&#8216;379 patent&#8221;), 8,329,752&#160;(the &#8220;&#8216;752 patent&#8221;), 8,362,085&#160;(the &#8220;&#8216;085 patent&#8221;), and&#160;8,598,233 (the &#8220;&#8216;233 patent&#8221;) in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware against Wockhardt, Teva, Sun, Apotex, Anchen, Zydus, Watson, Par, Mylan, Amneal, Ranbaxy,&#160;and Amerigen, and related subsidiaries and affiliates thereof. Plaintiffs entered settlement agreements with every defendant except Teva. </font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On December 11, 2017, the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit issued a decision affirming the district court&#8217;s judgment of invalidity with respect to certain claims of the &#8216;209, &#8216;708, &#8216;379, &#8216;752 and &#8216;085 patents.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Federal Circuit issued the mandate of the court on February 20, 2018, and certain generics launched the generic products shortly thereafter.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU161"></a>Namzaric<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup><font style="font-style:normal;">. In 2015 subsidiaries of the Company and Adamas Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (all collectively, &#8220;Plaintiffs&#8221;), brought an action for infringement of some or all of U.S. Patent Nos. 8,039,009 (the &#8220;&#8217;009 patent&#8221;), 8,058,291 (the &#8220;&#8216;291 patent&#8221;), 8,168,209 (the &#8220;&#8216;209 patent&#8221;),&#160;8,173,708 (the &#8220;&#8216;708 patent&#8221;) 8,283,379 (the &#8220;&#8216;379 patent&#8221;),&#160;8,293,794 (the &#8220;&#8216;794 patent&#8221;), 8,329,752 (the &#8220;&#8216;752 patent&#8221;), 8,338,485 (the &#8220;&#8216;485 patent&#8221;), 8,338,486 (the &#8220;&#8216;486 patent&#8221;), 8,362,085 (the &#8220;&#8216;085 patent&#8221;), 8,580,858 (the &#8220;&#8216;858 patent&#8221;) and&#160;8,598,233 (the &#8220;&#8216;233 patent&#8221;) in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware against Amneal Pharmaceuticals LLC, Par Pharmaceutical, Inc., and Amerigen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. and Amerigen Pharmaceuticals Ltd. (collectively, &#8220;Amerigen&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Plaintiffs entered into settlement agreements with each of the generics.&nbsp;&nbsp;Plaintiffs&#8217; settlement agreement with Amneal, who is believed to be a first applicant with respect to certain dosage strengths (memantine hydrochloride extended-release and donepezil hydrochloride, 14 mg/10 mg and 28 mg/10 mg) of Namzaric<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>., provides a license to Amneal that will permit it to launch its generic version of Namzaric<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;as of January 1, 2025, or earlier in certain circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;Alternatively, under certain circumstances, Amneal has an </font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-83</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-style:normal;">option to launch an authorized generic version of Namzaric beginning on January 1, 2026.&nbsp;&nbsp;No patent litigation remains concerning Namzaric.</font><font style="font-style:normal;"> </font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup><font style="font-style:normal;">. Between August 2015 and July 2016, a subsidiary of the Company brought actions for infringement of U.S. Patent Nos. 8,629,111 (the &#8220;&#8216;111 patent&#8221;), 8,633,162 (the &#8220;&#8216;162 patent&#8221;), 8,642,556 (the &#8220;&#8216;556 patent&#8221;), 8,648,048 (the &#8220;&#8216;048 patent&#8221;), 8,685,930 (the &#8220;&#8216;930 patent&#8221;) and 9,248,191 (the &#8220;&#8217;191 patent&#8221;) in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas against Akorn, Inc., Apotex, Inc., Mylan Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Teva Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc., InnoPharma, Inc., Famy Care Limited (&#8220;Famy Care&#8221;), TWi Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (&#8220;TWi&#8221;) and related subsidiaries and affiliates thereof. </font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The subsidiary entered into settlement agreements with Apotex, TWi, Famy Care and InnoPharma.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of certain of these settlements, Allergan will provide a license to certain parties to launch their generic versions of Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> beginning on February 27, 2024, or earlier in certain circumstances. Additionally, under certain circumstances, the Company will supply and authorize certain parties to launch an authorized generic version of Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> on August 28, 2024 or earlier in certain circumstances.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On September 8, 2017, the Company assigned all Orange Book-listed patents for Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174; </sup>to the Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe (&#8220;the Tribe&#8221;), a recognized sovereign tribal government, and concurrently was granted an exclusive field-of-use license to practice the patents in the United States for all FDA-approved uses of the products under the Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> NDAs. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_Hlk529872494"></a><a name="_Hlk529872494"></a>On October 16, 2017, the District Court issued a decision and final judgment finding that the asserted claims of the &#8216;111 patent, the &#8216;048 patent, the &#8216;930 patent and the &#8216;191 patent were infringed, but invalid on the ground of obviousness. The District Court also held that the asserted claims were not invalid as anticipated, for lack of enablement, or for improper inventorship.  On November 13, 2018, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit issued a decision affirming the district court&#8217;s finding of invalidity of the asserted claims of the &#8216;111, &#8216;048, &#8216;930 and &#8216;191 Patents.&nbsp;&nbsp;A petition for rehearing is currently pending.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_Hlk529872555"></a>On December 22, 2016, a subsidiary of the Company <a name="_Hlk529872555"></a>Allergan filed a complaint for infringement of the &#700;111&#160;patent, &#700;162&#160;patent, &#700;556&#160;patent, &#700;048&#160;patent, &#700;930&#160;patent, and the &#700;191&#160;patent in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas against Deva Holding A.S. (&#8220;Deva&#8221;). On March 6, 2018, the district court granted in part and denied in part the parties&#8217; joint motion for entry of a stipulated order, and stayed the case until such time as the Federal Circuit in the lead appeal case with Teva, Mylan and Akron issues a mandate. The parties&#8217; stipulation provides that Deva will be bound by the outcome of that appeal.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On August 10 and September 20, 2018, a subsidiary of the Company and the Tribe filed complaints for infringement of the &#700;162&#160;patent and the &#700;556&#160;patent in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware against Saptalis and against Amneal Pharmaceuticals, LLC and Amneal Pharmaceuticals Co. India Private Limited (collectively, &#8220;Amneal&#8221;), respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The cases were voluntarily dismissed on January 2, 2019.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;IPR.<font style="font-style:normal;">&#160;On June&#160;6, 2016, a subsidiary of the Company received&#160;notification letters that Inter Partes Review of the USPTO (&#8220;IPR&#8221;) petitions were filed by Mylan Pharmaceuticals Inc. (&#8220;Mylan&#8221;) regarding U.S. Patent Nos.&#160;8,629,111 (the &#8220;&#8216;111 patent&#8221;), 8,633,162 (the &#8220;&#8216;162 patent&#8221;), 8,642,556 (the &#8220;&#8216;556 patent&#8221;), 8,648,048 (the &#8220;&#8216;048 patent&#8221;), 8,685,930 (the &#8220;&#8216;930 patent&#8221;), and 9,248,191 (the &#8220;&#8216;191 patent&#8221;), which patents expire on August&#160;27, 2024. Mylan filed the IPR petition on June&#160;3, 2016. On June&#160;23, 2016, a subsidiary of the Company received a notification letter that a IPR petition and motion for joinder was filed by Argentum Pharmaceuticals LLC (&#8220;Argentum&#8221;) regarding the &#8217;111 patent.&nbsp;&nbsp;On December 7, 2016, the Company entered into a settlement agreement with Argentum and Argentum&#8217;s petition was withdrawn.&nbsp;&nbsp;On December 8, 2016, the USPTO granted Mylan&#8217;s petitions to institute IPRs with respect to these patents. On January 6, 2017, each of Akorn and Teva filed, and on January 9, 2017 the USPTO received, IPR petitions with respect to these patents and motions for joinder with the Mylan IPR. The USPTO granted Teva&#8217;s and Akorn&#8217;s joinder motions on March 31, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On September 8, 2017, Allergan assigned all Orange Book-listed patents for Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174; </sup>to the Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe (&#8220;the Tribe&#8221;), a recognized sovereign tribal government, and concurrently was granted an exclusive field-of-use license to practice the patents in the United States for all FDA-approved uses of the products under the Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> NDAs. That same day, the Tribe filed an updated Mandatory Notice with the USPTO to reflect that the Tribe is the patent owner, and sought permission to file a motion to dismiss based on tribal sovereign immunity. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On February 23, 2018, the USPTO issued orders denying the Tribe&#8217;s motion to dismiss (or terminate).&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On July 20, 2018, the Federal Circuit affirmed the USPTO&#8217;s denial of the Tribe&#8217;s motion to dismiss and Allergan&#8217;s motion to withdraw.&nbsp;&nbsp;On August 20, 2018, the Tribe and Allergan filed a petition for rehearing <font style="font-style:italic;">en banc</font>, which the Federal Circuit denied on October 22, 2018. On December 21, 2018, the Company and the Tribe filed a petition for a writ of certiorari with the United States Supreme Court.&nbsp;&nbsp;That petition is currently pending.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-84</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU162"></a><font style="font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Saphris</font><font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font><font style="font-style:normal;">. Between September 2014 and May 2015, </font><font style="font-style:normal;">subsidiaries of the Company </font><font style="font-style:normal;">brought actions for infringement of some or all of U.S. Patent Nos.&#160;5,763,476 (the &#8220;&#8216;476 patent&#8221;), 7,741,358 (the &#8220;&#8216;358 patent&#8221;) and 8,022,228 (the &#8220;&#8216;228 patent&#8221;) against Sigmapharm Laboratories, LLC, Hikma Pharmaceuticals, LLC, Breckenridge Pharmaceutical, Inc., Alembic Pharmaceuticals, Ltd. and Amneal Pharmaceuticals, LLC, and related subsidiaries and affiliates thereof</font><font style="font-style:normal;"> </font><font style="font-style:normal;">in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware</font><font style="font-style:normal;"> </font><font style="font-style:normal;">in connection with an abbreviated new drug applications respectively filed with FDA by Sigmpha Hikma, Breckenridge, Alembic and Amneal, each seeking approval to market a generic versions of Saphris and challenging each of said patents</font><font style="font-style:normal;">. Including a 6-month pediatric extension of regulatory exclusivity, the &#8216;476 patent expires in December 2020, and the &#8216;358 and &#8216;228 patents expire in October 2026. </font><font style="font-style:normal;">In 2016, the parties agreed to dismiss all </font><font style="font-style:normal;">claims related to the &#8216;358 and &#8216;228 patents</font><font style="font-style:normal;">, leaving only the &#8216;476 patent at issue.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-style:normal;">On October 13, 2016, the court stayed trial as to Sigmapharm and extended the 30-month stay as to Sigmapharm.&nbsp;&nbsp;On June 30, 2017, the district court issued an opinion and order finding all asserted claims of the &#8216;476 patent valid, and that claims 4, 9 and 10 were not infringed by Alembic and Breckenridge.&nbsp;&nbsp;On July 11, 2017, the district court entered a final judgment that ordered, among other things, that Alembic&#8217;s, Amneal&#8217;s, Breckenridge&#8217;s and Hikma&#8217;s respective ANDAs not be granted final approval by FDA earlier than the date of expiration of the &#8216;476 patent inclusive of any applicable adjustments, extensions or exclusivities. </font><font style="font-style:normal;"> The case is currently on appeal.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A separate bench trial concerning Sigmapharm&#8217;s infringement of the &#8216;476 patent began on June 20, 2018, and on November 16, 2018, the court held that Sigmapharms&#8217; proposed ANDA product would infringe the &#8216;476 patent &nbsp;&nbsp;On November 26, 2018, Sigmapharm sought relief from the November 16, 2018 decision.&nbsp;&nbsp;That motion is currently pending.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Savella<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>. <font style="font-style:normal;">On October 5 and 6, 2017, subsidiaries of the Company brought actions for infringement of U.S. Patent Nos. 6,602,911 (the &#8220;&#8216;911 patent&#8221;),&#160;7,888,342 (the &#8220;&#8216;342 patent&#8221;), and&#160;7,994,220 (the &#8220;&#8216;220 patent&#8221;) in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware and the District of New Jersey, respectively, against Strides Pharma Global Pte Limited and Strides Pharma Inc. (collectively, Strides&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;On April 20, 2018, the Company entered into a settlement agreement with Strides and the case was dismissed.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Viibryd<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;IPR.<font style="font-style:normal;">&#160;On January 5, 2018, Argentum Pharmaceuticals LLC submitted to the USPTO a petition for Inter Partes Review (&#8220;IPR&#8221;) seeking cancellation of certain claims of U.S. Patent No.&#160;8,673,921 (the &#8220;&#8216;921 patent&#8221;). The &#8216;921 patent is listed in the Orange Book for Viibryd<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> and expires in June 2022.  On July 23, 2018, the USPTO denied institution of the IPR.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Trademark Enforcement Matters</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Juv&#233;derm<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font>.<font style="font-style:normal;">&#160; </font>&#160;&#160;<font style="font-style:normal;">On April 5, 2017, a subsidiary of the Company brought an action for unfair competition, false advertising, dilution, conspiracy and infringement of Allergan&#8217;s JUV&#201;DERM trademarks in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California against Dermavita Limited Partnership (&#8220;Dermavita&#8221;), Dima Corp. S.A. &#160;(&#8220;Dima Corp.&#8221;) and KBC Media Relations LLC (&#8220;KBC&#8221;).&#160;Dima Corp. had previously announced its acquisition of a license from Dermavita to develop and market in the U.S. cosmetic products under the Juvederm trademark.&#160;During June 2017, the Company entered into a settlement agreement with KBC.&#160;During July 2017, the Court preliminarily enjoined Dima Corp. from, </font>inter alia<font style="font-style:normal;">, promoting or selling within the United States any product bearing the trademark JUVEDERM or any other trademark confusingly similar to it.&#160;During January 2018, the Court granted Dermavita&#8217;s renewed motion to dismiss the Company&#8217;s complaint based on purported lack of personal jurisdiction.&nbsp;&nbsp;The case remains pending against Dima.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Subsidiaries of the Company requested a preliminary injunction against Dermavita, Dima Corp, Aesthetic Services, Jacqueline Sillam and Dimitri Sillam in the High Court of Paris, France.&#160;During June 2017, the Paris Court preliminarily enjoined the defendants<font style="font-style:italic;">, inter alia</font>, to refrain from promoting or selling in France its Juvederm products, to transfer various domain names and to pay provisional damages to Allergan, on the basis that such use would infringe Allergan&#8217;s EU and French JUV&#201;DERM trademarks and would amount to unfair competition. This injunction has been appealed.&#160;A subsidiary of the Company has also filed against Dermavita, Dima Corp. and others a full action of trademark infringement in the Paris court.&#160;Dermavita has requested that the full action be stayed pending the outcome of the Nanterre action and the EUIPO trademark proceedings, both mentioned below.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Paris court rejected Dermavita&#8217;s stay request and subsequently ordered the defendants to pay more than 75,000 Euros in liquidated damages for violation of the preliminary injunction mentioned above.&nbsp;&nbsp;Dermavita has filed an action against subsidiaries of the Company in the Nanterre, France court alleging that the subsidiaries have not used its JUV&#201;DERM trademark and requesting the court to revoke the Company&#8217;s trademark based on its purported lack of use.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has submitted its principal brief and awaits a hearing on. &#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Furthermore, more than 150 trademark opposition and cancellation actions between Allergan and Dermavita have been filed in front of the USPTO, EUIPO and various other national and regional trademark offices around the world.&nbsp;&nbsp;Most of these actions remain pending; however, Allergan has received favorable decisions in more than ten (10) such actions.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-85</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU163"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Antitrust Litigation</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Asacol<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font>&#160;Litigation.<font style="font-style:normal;">&#160;Class action complaints have been filed against certain subsidiaries of the Company on behalf of putative classes of direct and indirect purchasers.&#160;The lawsuits have been consolidated in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts.&nbsp;&nbsp;The complaints allege that plaintiffs paid higher prices for Asacol<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;HD and Delzicol<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;as a result of alleged actions preventing or delaying generic competition in the market for an older Asacol<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;product in violation of U.S. federal antitrust laws and/or state laws. Plaintiffs seek unspecified injunctive relief, treble damages and/or attorneys&#8217; fees.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has settled the claims brought by the direct purchaser plaintiffs.&nbsp;&nbsp;While the district court granted the indirect purchaser plaintiffs&#8217; motion for class certification, the Court of Appeals for the First Circuit issued an order granting the Company&#8217;s motion to appeal the district court&#8217;s decision to certify the proposed class and later issued a decision reversing the lower court&#8217;s decision on class certification.&nbsp;&nbsp;The appellate court recently denied plaintiffs&#8217; motion for rehearing </font>en banc<font style="font-style:normal;">.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Botox<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font>&#160;Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">. A class action complaint was filed against certain subsidiaries of the Company in the United States District Court for the Central District of  California on February&#160;24, 2015,&nbsp;&nbsp;alleging unlawful market allocation in violation of Section&#160;1 of the Sherman Act, 15 U.S.C. &#167;1, agreement in restraint of trade in violation of  the U.S. federal antitrust laws as well as violations of California state laws. In the complaint, plaintiffs seek an unspecified amount of treble damages.&#160;&#160; On November 30, 2017, the parties reached a tentative settlement and the court granted plaintiffs&#8217; motion for final approval of class settlement.&nbsp;&nbsp;On September 10, 2018, the court dismissed with prejudice all claims against the defendants.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loestrin<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font>&#160;24 Litigation.<font style="font-style:normal;">&#160;Putative classes of direct and indirect purchasers as well as opt-out direct purchasers have filed complaints that have been consolidated in the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island.&nbsp;&nbsp;The lawsuits allege that subsidiaries of the Company engaged in anticompetitive conduct, including when settling patent lawsuits related to Loestrin</font><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup><font style="font-style:normal;"> 24 Fe, in violation of federal and state antitrust and consumer protection laws. The complaints each seek declaratory and injunctive relief and damages. The court has scheduled hearings on the class plaintiffs&#8217; class certification motions and on defendants motion for summary judgement on the issue of market power.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Namenda<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font>&#160;Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">.&#160;In 2014, the State of New York filed a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York alleging that Forest was acting to prevent or delay generic competition to Namenda<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;in violation of federal and New York antitrust laws and committed other fraudulent acts in connection with its commercial plans for Namenda<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;XR. The district court granted the state&#8217;s motion for a preliminary injunction which was later affirmed by the Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit.&nbsp;&nbsp;The parties in that case then reached a settlement to resolve the dispute.  Following the conclusion of the New York Attorney General Matter, putative class actions were filed on behalf of direct and indirect purchasers in the same federal court.&#160;The class action complaints make claims similar to those asserted by the New York Attorney General and also include claims that Namenda<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;patent litigation settlements between a Company subsidiary and generic companies also violated the antitrust laws. Plaintiffs seek unspecified injunctive relief, treble damages and attorneys&#8217; fees.&nbsp;&nbsp;The court has denied defendants&#8217; motion for summary judgement in the direct purchaser action and has certified the direct purchaser class of plaintiffs.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Restasis<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font> Competitor Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">.&#160; Shire, which offers the dry-eye disease drug Xiidra<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>, sued subsidiaries of the Company in U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey alleging that defendants unlawfully harmed competition by foreclosing Xiidra<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> from sales to Medicare Part D plans (and the members of such plans) through the use of discounts (a) contingent on Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> receiving<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top"> </sup>preferential formulary treatment; and/or (b) across a bundle of Allergan&#8217;s products, including Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>.&#160; The complaint seeks injunctive relief and damages under federal and state law.&nbsp;&nbsp;The court has yet to rule on defendants&#8217; motion to dismiss the complaint and the parties are engaged in limited discovery.&#160; </font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Restasis<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font> Class Action Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">.&#160; Several class actions were filed on behalf of putative classes of direct and indirect purchasers of Restasis</font><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup><font style="font-style:normal;"> alleging that subsidiaries of the company harmed competition by engaging in conduct to delay the market entry of generic versions of Restasis<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top"> </sup>in violation of the federal antitrust laws as well as state antitrust and consumer-protection laws and unjust enrichment.&#160; The cases have been consolidated in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey.&nbsp;&nbsp;All plaintiffs seek damages, declaratory relief, and injunctive relief.&#160;&#160; The parties are currently engaged in discovery.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-86</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU164"></a><font style="font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Commercial Litigation</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Celexa<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font>/Lexapro<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font>&#160;Class Actions<font style="font-style:normal;">.&#160;Certain subsidiaries of the Company were named in federal court actions relating to the promotion of Celexa<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;and/or Lexapro<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;all of which were consolidated in an&#160;MDL proceeding in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts. Most of these claims were resolved through a settlement in September 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, two lawsuits remain which assert claims under the federal Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (&#8220;RICO&#8221;) Act.&#160; The court has entered summary judgment in favor of the defendants in both actions and denied plaintiffs&#8217; class certification motions.&#160;&#160; Plaintiffs in both cases appealed the dismissal of their claims and denial of class certification to the United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit and the appeals court issued a decision in January 2019 affirming the denial of the class certification motions but reversing the lower court&#8217;s decision granting the defendants&#8217; summary judgment motions.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Warner Chilcott Marketing Practices<font style="font-style:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;A putative nationwide class of private payer entities, or their assignees, that paid Medicare benefits on behalf of their beneficiaries filed a complaint against certain subsidiaries of the Company in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts. The Complaint asserts claims under the federal RICO statute, state&#160;consumer protection statutes,&#160;common law fraud, and unjust enrichment with respect to the sale and marketing of certain products. Defendants&#8217; motion to dismiss the Amended Complaint is still pending.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Generic Drug Pricing Securities and ERISA Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Putative classes of&nbsp;&nbsp;shareholders and two individual opt-out plaintiffs filed class action lawsuits&nbsp;&nbsp;against the Company and certain of its current and former officers alleging that defendants made materially false and misleading statements between February 2014 and November 2016 regarding the Company&#8217;s internal controls over its financial reporting and that it failed to disclose that its former Actavis generics unit had engaged in illegal, anticompetitive price-fixing with its generic industry peers.&nbsp;&nbsp;These lawsuits have been consolidated in the U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey. The complaints seek unspecified monetary damages.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#8217;s motion to dismiss the complaint is still pending.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, class action complaints have been filed premised on the same alleged underlying conduct that is at issue in the securities litigation but that assert claims under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (&#8220;ERISA&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;These complaints have been consolidated in the district court in New Jersey.&#160; The court granted the Company&#8217;s motion to dismiss this complaint.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ERISA plaintiffs have appealed this decision to the Third Circuit Court of Appeals.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Telephone Consumer Protection Act Litigation.<font style="font-style:normal;">&#160; In October 2012, Forest and certain of its affiliates were named as defendants in a putative class action in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Missouri. This suit alleges that Forest and another defendant violated the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (the &#8220;TCPA&#8221;) by sending unsolicited facsimiles and facsimiles with inadequate opt-out notices.&nbsp;&nbsp;The case was stayed pending the administrative proceeding initiated by the pending FCC Petition and a separate petition Forest filed. A similar lawsuit was filed in in Missouri state court against Warner Chilcott Corporation which Warner Chilcott removed to the federal district court. In the wake of the Court of Appeals decision on the Petition discussed below, the parties reached an agreement to settle these actions.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In a related matter, on June&#160;27, 2013, Forest filed a Petition for Declaratory Ruling with the FCC requesting that the FCC find that (1)&#160;the faxes at issue in the action complied, or substantially complied with the FCC regulation, and thus did not violate it, or (2)&#160;the FCC regulation was not properly promulgated under the TCPA. On October&#160;30, 2014, the FCC issued a final order on the FCC Petition granting Forest and several other petitioners a retroactive waiver of the opt-out notice requirement for all faxes sent with express consent. The litigation plaintiffs appealed the final order to the Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia and on March 31, 2017, the Court of Appeals issued a decision which held that the FCC regulation at issue was not properly promulgated under the TCPA.&nbsp;&nbsp;Plaintiffs&#8217; petition for certiorari was denied by the United States Supreme Court.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Prescription Opioid Drug Abuse Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">.&#160;The Company has been named as a defendant, along with several other manufacturers and distributors of opioid products, in over 1,300 matters relating to the promotion and sale of prescription opioid pain relievers and additional suits have been filed.&nbsp;&nbsp;The lawsuits allege generally that the manufacturer defendants engaged in a deceptive campaign to promote their products in violation of state laws and seek unspecified monetary damages, penalties and injunctive relief.&nbsp;&nbsp;Plaintiffs in these suits include states, political subdivisions of states (i.e., counties and municipalities), Native American tribes and other private litigants such as insurance plans, hospital systems and consumers who were prescribed opioid products and were subsequently treated for an overdose or addiction.&nbsp;&nbsp;Cases are pending in both federal and state courts.&nbsp;&nbsp;The federal court cases have been consolidated in an MDL in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio, with a first set of cases set for trial in September 2019.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the case filed on behalf of the State of California by the California counties of Santa Clara and Orange, which is pending in California state court, the previously-set trial date has been vacated and a new date has not yet been set.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-87</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU165"></a><font style="font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Testosterone Replacement Therapy Class Action</font><font style="font-style:normal;">.&#160;</font><font style="font-style:normal;">Subsidiaries of </font><font style="font-style:normal;">the Company </font><font style="font-style:normal;">were named in a </font><font style="font-style:normal;">class action complaint filed on behalf a </font><font style="font-style:normal;">putative </font><font style="font-style:normal;">class of third party payers in </font><font style="font-style:normal;">the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of</font><font style="font-style:normal;"> Illinois. The suit alleges that the Company</font><font style="font-style:normal;">&#8217;s subsidiaries</font><font style="font-style:normal;"> violated various laws including the federal RICO statute and state consumer protection laws in connection with the sale and marketing of Androderm</font><font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font><font style="font-style:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-style:normal;">The class p</font><font style="font-style:normal;">laintiff</font><font style="font-style:normal;">s</font><font style="font-style:normal;"> seek to obtain certain equitable relief, including injunctive relief and an order requiring restitution and/or disgorgement, and to recover damages and multiple damages in an unspecified amount. </font><font style="font-style:normal;">While the lawsuit is ongoing, </font><font style="font-style:normal;">the court </font><font style="font-style:normal;">has denied </font><font style="font-style:normal;">plaintiff&#8217;s class certification motion</font><font style="font-style:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Defendants</font><font style="font-style:normal;">&#8217;</font><font style="font-style:normal;"> motion for summary judgment</font><font style="font-style:normal;"> is still pending</font><font style="font-style:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Xaleron Dispute.&#160;<font style="font-style:normal;">On February&#160;5, 2016, Xaleron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. filed a lawsuit against certain subsidiaries of the Company in state court in New York. The complaint, filed on February&#160;26, 2016, alleges the defendants misappropriated&#160;Xaleron&#8217;s confidential business information and asserts claims for unfair competition, tortious interference with prospective economic advantage and unjust enrichment.&#160;The company filed a motion for summary judgment in April 2018 and subsequently,&nbsp;&nbsp;the parties reached an agreement to settle the litigation.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Zeltiq Advertising Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;A putative class action lawsuit was filed against Zeltiq in state court in California alleging that Zeltiq misled customers regarding the promotion of its CoolSculpting</font><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup><font style="font-style:normal;"> product and the product&#8217;s premarket notification clearance status.&nbsp;&nbsp;The case was later removed to U.S. District Court for the Central District of California.&nbsp;&nbsp;The case was dismissed by the district court and, while the plaintiffs started the process of appealing this decision to the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals, they have since voluntarily dismissed their appeal.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employment Litigation</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In July 2012, a subsidiary of the Company was named as a defendant in an action brought by certain former Company sales representatives and specialty sales representatives in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York. The action is a putative class and collective action, and alleges class claims under Title VII for gender discrimination with respect to pay and promotions, as well as discrimination on the basis of pregnancy, and a collective action claim under the Equal Pay Act and non-class claims on behalf of certain of the named Plaintiffs for sexual harassment and retaliation under Title VII, and for violations of the Family and Medical Leave Act.&#160;&nbsp;&nbsp;On April 3, 2017, the parties agreed to settle this matter.&nbsp;&nbsp;On February 1, 2018, the court granted preliminary approval of the settlement and set a fairness hearing for May 4, 2018. On June 29, 2018, the Court granted final approval of the settlement.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Product Liability Litigation</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Actonel<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font>&#160;Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">.&#160;A subsidiary of the Company is a defendant in over 500 filed cases in federal and various state courts, relating to the bisphosphonate prescription drug Actonel<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>.&#160; In addition, there are three cases pending in provincial courts in Canada, two involving single plaintiffs, and a third on behalf of a purported class of injured plaintiffs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The complaints allege, among other things, that Actonel<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;caused them to suffer osteonecrosis of the jaw (&#8220;ONJ&#8221;) and/or atypical fractures of the femur.&nbsp;&nbsp;Plaintiffs are seeking unspecified monetary and injunctive relief, as well as attorneys&#8217; fees. The Company subsidiary is being indemnified by Sanofi for certain claims pursuant to an agreement with Sanofi and is being partially indemnified by the Procter&#160;&amp; Gamble Company (&#8220;P&amp;G&#8221;) for ONJ claims that were pending at the time the Company subsidiary acquired P&amp;G&#8217;s global pharmaceutical business in 2009. Settlements have been reached that have resolved most of the pending ONJ-related claims. Recently, all pending Actonel cases in New Jersey state court were dismissed without prejudice subject to refilling after the U.S. Supreme Court issues a decision in </font>Merck Sharp &amp; Dohme Corp. v. Albrecht<font style="font-style:normal;">, Doc. No. 17-290.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Breast Implant Litigation.<font style="font-style:normal;"> Certain Company subsidiaries are defendants in more than a dozen cases alleging that Allergan&#8217;s textured breast implants caused women to develop a rare condition known as anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL), and that the defendants failed to properly warn against this risk and failed to promptly and properly report the results of the post-marketing studies relating to these products.&nbsp;&nbsp;These cases have been filed in both federal and state courts in the United States and well as provincial courts in Canada.&nbsp;&nbsp;One of the Canadian cases has been asserted on behalf a putative class of consumers.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Benicar<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;Litigation.<font style="font-style:normal;">&#160;A subsidiary of the Company has been named in a number of lawsuits involving allegations that Benicar<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup> caused certain gastrointestinal injuries.&#160;Under a co-promotion agreement, Daiichi Sankyo is defending the Company subsidiary in these lawsuits and has announced that it has agreed to enter into a program to settle all of the pending cases on behalf of all defendants, including the Company subsidiary.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Celexa<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>/Lexapro<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain Company subsidiaries are defendants in over 150 actions alleging that Celexa<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;or Lexapro<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>&#160;caused various birth defects.&#160;Several of the cases involve multiple minor-plaintiffs. The majority of these actions have been consolidated in state court in Missouri; none of the actions are set for trial.&#160;</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-88</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU166"></a><font style="font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">RepliForm</font><font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font><font style="font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> Litigation.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-style:normal;">A Company subsidiary has been named as a defendant in over 300 cases alleging that its biologic mesh product RepliForm</font><font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font><font style="font-style:normal;"> did not perform as intended and caused various injuries.&nbsp;&nbsp;The majority of these cases have been consolidated in state court in Massachusetts, with the rest pending in state courts in Delaware and Minnesota and the federal court in West Virginia. Approximately 200 of these cases have been settled or dismissed.</font><font style="font-style:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Testosterone Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">. A number of product liability suits were filed against certain Company subsidiaries as well as other manufacturers and distributors of testosterone products, for personal injuries including but not limited to cardiovascular events allegedly arising out of the use of Androderm<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup>.&nbsp;&nbsp;The cases have been consolidated in an MDL in the U.S. District Court for Northern District of Illinois.&nbsp;&nbsp;In mid-2018, the parties reached an agreement to settle all of the pending cases.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Government Investigations, Government Litigation and Qui Tam Litigation </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company and its subsidiaries are involved in various disputes, governmental and/or regulatory inspections, inquires, investigations and proceedings that could result in litigation, and other litigation matters that arise from time to time. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Company subsidiaries have received subpoenas and/or Civil Investigative Demands (&#8220;CID&#8221;) from the United States Department of Justice, the United States Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General, United States Congressional Committees as well as various state regulatory and enforcement authorities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Each of the subpoenas and CIDs seek documents and information relating to discrete topics, including but not limited to: the calculation and reporting by certain Company subsidiaries of their Average Manufacturer Prices, Average Wholesale Prices and Best Prices for several of their products; sales and marketing practices of Botox to urology practices; the promotion and sale of two gastroenterology products; the Saint Regis Mohawk Tribe&#8217;s acquisition of six Restasis patents and the granting of exclusive licenses to the Restasis product to the Company; and, the promotion and sale of opioid products.&#160;In each case, the Company and its subsidiaries are cooperating fully with the governmental authority&#8217;s requests.&nbsp;&nbsp; </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain states have initiated lawsuits and <font style="font-style:italic;">qui tam</font> lawsuits have been filed by private parties, also known as relators, on behalf of the federal or state governments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain Company subsidiaries have been named as defendants in lawsuits that allege generally that state Medicaid agencies were overcharged for their share of Medicaid drug reimbursement costs due to inflated Average Wholesale Prices (&#8220;AWP&#8221;) reported by the Company subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;AWP lawsuits are currently pending in Illinois, Utah and Wisconsin.</p>
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Matters Relating to the Company&#8217;s Divested Generics Business</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following matters relate to the former generics business of the Company or the transaction pursuant to which that business was sold to Teva, effective August 2, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp; Teva has agreed to indemnify and defend the Company against all matters asserted in litigation against the Company arising out of the former generics business, including litigations and investigations relating to generic opioid products including, without limitation, the actions described below.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Lidoderm<font style="font-style:normal;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">&#174;</sup></font> Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The U.S. Federal Trade Commission filed a lawsuit in federal district court in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania against the Company and one of its former global generics business subsidiaries and others alleging that patent litigation settlements relating to Lidoderm were anticompetitive. The FTC voluntarily withdrew its complaint in Pennsylvania and filed a similar complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District California where similar lawsuits filed by private plaintiffs were already pending and where the State of California filed a similar complaint against the same defendants.&nbsp;&nbsp; Defendants in the Pennsylvania action filed a declaratory judgment action against the FTC in the Pennsylvania federal court but the court granted the FTC&#8217;s motion to dismiss this lawsuit.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FTC and State of California&#8217;s actions were stayed pending the declaratory judgment action in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.&nbsp;&nbsp;The federal court in California has not yet issued a ruling or lifted the stay in these cases since the court&#8217;s ruling in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Hydrocortisone Investigation<font style="font-style:normal;">. In 2016, the Company received notice from the UK Competition and Markets Authority (&#8220;CMA&#8221;) that it would be included within the scope of the CMA&#8217;s formal investigation under Section&#160;25 of the Competition Act of 1998 (&#8220;CA98&#8221;) into suspected abuse of dominance by a former generics business subsidiary of the Company in relation to the supply of 10mg and 20mg hydrocortisone tablets. The CMA is investigating: (i) alleged excessive and unfair prices with respect to hydrocortisone tablets and (ii) whether the former generics business subsidiary entered into anti-competitive agreements with a potential competitor for this product.&nbsp;&nbsp;The CMA has issued statements of objection with respect to both parts of its investigation. The Company intends to cooperate fully with the investigation.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Teva Shareholder Derivative Litigation<font style="font-style:normal;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2017, the Company was named as defendant in a proposed Teva shareholder derivative litigation filed in the Economic Division of the Tel Aviv District Court in Israel.&nbsp;&nbsp;The lawsuit contains allegations that the Company aided and abetted Teva&#8217;s board of directors violations of Israeli securities laws.&nbsp;&nbsp;To date, the court has not determined whether it will allow plaintiffs to proceed with this action.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-89</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTE 26 &#8212; Warner Chilcott Limited (&#8220;WCL&#8221;) Guarantor and Non-Guarantor Condensed Consolidating Financial Information</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following financial information is presented to segregate the financial results of WCL, Allergan Funding SCS, and Allergan Finance, LLC (the issuers of the long-term notes), the guarantor subsidiaries for the long-term notes and the non-guarantor subsidiaries. The guarantors jointly and severally, and fully and unconditionally, guarantee the Company&#8217;s obligation under the long-term notes.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The information includes elimination entries necessary to consolidate the guarantor and the non-guarantor subsidiaries. Investments in subsidiaries are accounted for using the equity method of accounting. The principal elimination entries eliminate investments in subsidiaries, equity and intercompany balances and transactions.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">WCL, Allergan Capital S.a.r.l. and Allergan Finance, LLC are guarantors of the long-term notes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company anticipates future legal entity structure changes which may impact the presentation of this footnote in the near future.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">WCL has revised its consolidating balance sheets as previously presented in its balance sheet in Footnote 25 of the December 31, 2017 Annual Report on Form 10-K due to a change in the Company&#8217;s legal entity structure and other reclassifications that occurred during the year ended December 31, 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, prior period information has been recast to conform to the current period presentation.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Subsequent to December 31, 2018, Allergan&#8217;s legal entity structure changed which will result in reclassifications to the presented amounts in the year ending December 31, 2019.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following financial information presents the consolidating balance sheets as of December&#160;31, 2018 and 2017, the related statements of operations and comprehensive income / (loss) for the years ended December&#160;31, 2018, 2017 and 2016 and the statements of cash flows for the years ended December&#160;31, 2018, 2017 and 2016. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-90</a></p>

<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">No other country outside the U.S. and Canada had 10% or more of global sales.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s accounts receivable primarily arise from product sales in North America and primarily represent amounts due from wholesalers, distributors, drug store chains and service providers in the health care and pharmaceutical industries, public hospitals and other government entities. Approximately 62% and 58% of the gross accounts receivable balance are concentrated among the Company&#8217;s three largest customers as of December&#160;31, 2018 and 2017, respectively. The Company performs ongoing credit evaluations of its customers and maintains an allowance for potential uncollectible accounts. Actual losses from uncollectible accounts have been minimal.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Outside of the U.S., concentrations of credit risk with respect to accounts receivable are limited due to the wide variety of customers and markets using the Company&#8217;s products, as well as their dispersion across many different geographic areas.&#160;The Company monitors economic conditions, including volatility associated with international economies, and related impacts on the relevant financial markets and its business, especially in light of sovereign credit issues. The Company does not expect to have write-offs or adjustments to accounts receivable which would have a material adverse effect on its financial position, liquidity or results of operations.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain of the Company&#8217;s finished products and raw materials are obtained from single source suppliers. Although the Company seeks to identify more than one source for its various finished products and raw materials, loss of a single source supplier could have an adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s results of operations, financial condition and cash flows. Further, a second source supplier may not be able to produce the same volumes of inventory as the Company&#8217;s primary supplier. No third party manufacturer accounted for 10% or more of the Company&#8217;s products sold based on third-party revenues for the year ended December&#160;31, 2018.</p>
